name: FX cross-sectional momentum

origin.source_title: Currency momentum strategies (Journal of Financial Economics 106(3), 2012)

how_it_works.simple: Each month, buy the currencies that went up the most recently and sell the ones that went down the most, betting the leaders keep leading for a while.
how_it_works.analogy: Like a league table: back the teams at the top and bet against the teams at the bottom, and redraw the table every month.
how_it_works.precise: Currencies are sorted on lagged excess returns over a formation period f (1 to 12 months) into six portfolios, and the strategy is long the top sixth and short the bottom sixth for a holding period h. Menkhoff et al. (2012) find winners beat losers by up to 10 percent a year before costs, driven mostly by spot moves rather than interest differentials, and largely unrelated to carry and to moving average rules.

rule: At each month end, rank all available currencies by their excess return (spot change plus interest differential) over the last f months (f = 1 or 12 are common). Go long the top sixth (or top 3 of G10) and short the bottom sixth (or bottom 3) in equal weights and hold for one month.
data_needed: Spot exchange rates vs USD, month end
1-month forward rates or short interest rates
Bid-ask spreads (important: costs remove most of the profit)
economic_rationale: Menkhoff et al. (2012) find the returns are not explained by standard risk factors and look consistent with under- and over-reaction, but they are concentrated in currencies with high idiosyncratic volatility, high spreads and country risk, which limits arbitrage.
why_it_might_fail: Costs: with full quoted spreads the best 1-month strategy drops from 9.46 to 3.92 percent a year and many variants go negative (Menkhoff et al. 2012, Table 8). Chernov, Dahlquist and Lochstoer (2024) find G10 one-month momentum flattened out around 2000 and has a Sharpe near zero after costs over 1985-2023.

reported_results.market: Up to 48 currencies vs USD, long top sixth short bottom sixth
reported_results.notes: 1-month formation, 1-month holding, before costs. Turnover can exceed 70 percent per month.

reported_results.source: Menkhoff et al. (2012), Table 8, MOM(1,1) net
reported_results.notes: After full quoted bid-ask spreads. With 50 percent of quoted spreads (Table 9) it is 6.64 percent.

reported_results.source: Menkhoff et al. (2012), Tables 1 and 8, MOM(12,1)
reported_results.notes: 12-month formation, 1-month holding, before costs. After full quoted spreads the return is 1.40 percent a year (t = 0.74).

reported_results.source: Asness, Moskowitz, Pedersen (2013), Value and momentum everywhere, Table I (currency momentum P3-P1)
reported_results.market: 10 developed currencies, top third minus bottom third
reported_results.notes: 12-month momentum skipping the latest month. Correlation with currency value is -0.42.

reported_results.source: Chernov, Dahlquist, Lochstoer (2024), NBER WP 32900, Table 1 (CS-Mom 12, G10)
reported_results.notes: Before costs. After full quoted costs the Sharpe is -0.07. The 1-month version (CS-Mom 1) is 0.17 before costs and -0.07 after.

post_publication_evidence: Hutchinson et al. (2022) find the replicated currency carry, momentum and value strategies went from an average out-of-sample Sharpe of +0.39 to -0.32 after publication and that currency returns no longer show autocorrelation (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.irfa.2022.102245). Chernov, Dahlquist and Lochstoer (2024) report that G10 cross-sectional one-month momentum flattened around 2000 and broader samples around 2010.

implementations.notes: QuantConnect strategy library: 15 FX pairs 2006-2018, long 3 strongest and short 3 weakest on 12-month momentum vs USD. Needs the LEAN engine.
Replication and extension of Menkhoff et al. (2012) over 2000-2024 with transaction costs, using Datastream data. No license file.

relevance.reason: Well documented and easy to code, but in G10 after costs the recent evidence is close to zero, so it is more useful as a diversifier inside a combined portfolio than as a standalone S&P challenger.

research.notes: Implemented as `fx_xs_momentum` and run officially in RUN-000003, but no hypothesis doc yet, so the stage stays at 2 until one is written.
